issues.legal_issue: A subsequent suit for specific performance is not barred when it is founded on a cause of action distinct from that of an earlier suit for injunction and the plaintiff did not intentionally omit the later relief from the earlier suit.
material_facts: The earlier suit sought an injunction against threatened forcible dispossession and was founded on the defendant’s attempts to take possession of the property.

The later suit sought specific performance after the plaintiff learned that the housing authority had transferred the property to the defendant and the defendant denied, including in response to a legal notice, that he would perform the sale agreement.
The facts and evidence needed to support the injunction claim differed from those needed to support specific performance.
The Supreme Court found nothing in the earlier injunction plaint showing an intentional relinquishment of the specific-performance claim.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent specific-performance suit was not barred by Order 2 Rule 2 CPC. The High Court’s contrary finding was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Order 2 Rule 2 CPC requires a plaintiff to include the whole claim arising from the same cause of action, and bars a later suit for an omitted relief only where the later and earlier suits share the same cause of action and the plaintiff, being entitled to multiple reliefs, omitted the later relief without leave. The defendant must establish the precise cause of action in the earlier suit and its identity with that in the later suit; the bar is technical and cannot be presumed. A cause of action is the bundle of facts necessary to prove the right to judgment, and distinct causes may be shown where the evidence supporting the claims differs. The Court relied on Mohd. Khalil Khan v. Mahbub Ali Mian, Gurbux Singh v. Bhooralal, Kewal Singh v. Lajwanti, Deva Ram v. Ishwar Chand, Sidramappa v. Rajashetty, and State of M.P. v. State of Maharashtra. It distinguished Virgo Industries (Eng.) (P) Ltd. v. Venturetech Solutions (P) Ltd. on its facts and noted that precedent must be applied in the context of the facts of the case.

rule.if: subsequent_specific_performance_suit and earlier_injunction_suit and distinct_causes_of_action and not intentional_omission_of_later_relief

predicates.subsequent_specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a later proceeding seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.earlier_injunction_suit: The plaintiff had earlier brought a proceeding seeking an injunction against interference with possession or threatened dispossession.
predicates.distinct_causes_of_action: The earlier claim rested on facts about threatened dispossession, while the later claim rested on different facts giving rise to the demand for performance, such as disclosure of a transfer and refusal to perform.
predicates.intentional_omission_of_later_relief: The plaintiff intentionally left the later relief out of the earlier proceeding despite being entitled to seek it on the same cause of action.

issues.definition: When a later specific-performance suit follows an earlier injunction suit, the later suit is not barred if the claims arise from distinct causes of action and the plaintiff did not intentionally omit the later relief from the earlier suit.

issues.legal_issue: A first appellate court must decide all the points it has formulated for determination before disposing of the appeal.
material_facts: The High Court formulated several points for consideration but decided only the points concerning the procedural bar and the plaintiff’s conduct.
The High Court did not decide the remaining points, and the Supreme Court remitted the matter for their determination.
issues.conclusion: The matter was remanded to the High Court to decide the appeals and record findings on the remaining formulated points.
issues.legal_principle: A High Court acting as the final court of fact in a first appeal is required to decide all points it has formulated for consideration. The Supreme Court applied this appellate duty in ordering remand for decision of the outstanding points.

predicates.first_appeal: The proceeding before the court was a first appeal.
predicates.appellate_court_formulated_multiple_poin: The appellate court identified more than one point for consideration and decision.
predicates.appellate_court_failed_to_decide_all_poi: The appellate court disposed of the appeal without deciding every point it had formulated.

issues.definition: In a first appeal, if the appellate court formulates multiple points but leaves some undecided, the remaining points must be decided before the appeal is disposed of.
